cidr.description: IPv4 network in CIDR notation: four octets 0-255, a slash and a prefix length 0-32. Single hosts use /32.
cidr.markdownDescription:
IPv4 network in CIDR notation: four octets 0–255, a slash and a prefix length 0–32.

Single hosts use `/32`, for example `148.122.7.125/32`. `0.0.0.0/0` matches everything.
cidr.patternErrorMessage: Use IPv4 CIDR notation such as 213.75.0.0/16. Hosts need /32.

cidrList.description: One or more distinct IPv4 networks in CIDR notation.
cidrList.markdownDescription: One or more distinct IPv4 networks in CIDR notation.

country.description: A market the wizard offers as the first choice.
country.markdownDescription: A market the wizard offers as the first choice.

localName.description: Country name in its own language, shown next to the English name when it differs.
localName.markdownDescription: Country name in its own language, shown next to the English name when it differs, for example `Nederland`.

name.description: English country name shown in the wizard.
name.markdownDescription: English country name shown in the wizard, for example `Netherlands`.

countryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code in uppercase.
countryCode.markdownDescription: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code in uppercase, for example `NL`.
countryCode.patternErrorMessage: Use a two-letter uppercase ISO 3166-1 code, for example NL.

id.description: Lowercase identifier: a letter followed by 1 to 23 letters or digits. custom and legacy are reserved.
id.markdownDescription:
Lowercase identifier: a letter followed by 1 to 23 letters or digits.

`custom` and `legacy` are reserved for configurations without a profile.
id.patternErrorMessage: Use a lowercase letter followed by 1 to 23 lowercase letters or digits.

interface.description: Linux network interface name of 1 to 15 characters. Letters, digits, underscore, dot, colon and dash; may not start with a dot.
interface.markdownDescription:
Linux network interface name of 1 to 15 characters: letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `:` and `-`; may not start with a dot.

Examples: `eth8`, `ppp0`, `eth8.35`.
interface.patternErrorMessage: Use a Linux interface name of 1 to 15 characters, for example eth8 or ppp0.

label.description: Display text of 1 to 64 characters without leading or trailing whitespace.
label.markdownDescription: Display text of 1 to 64 characters without leading or trailing whitespace.

profile.description: Network settings for one IPTV network. Fields not listed here (proxy program, IGMP version, telemetry) come from the generic base; the WAN port and LAN bridges come from the console.
profile.markdownDescription:
Network settings for one IPTV network.

Fields not listed here (proxy `improxy`, IGMPv3, telemetry defaults, VLAN interface `iptv`) come from the generic base in Go and can be overridden by the user. The physical port and the LAN bridges come from the console.

name.description: Technical name shown only when a provider offers more than one profile.
name.markdownDescription: Technical name shown only when a provider offers more than one profile, for example `São Paulo network (VLAN 20, DHCP)`.

note.description: One sentence shown under the IPTV connection page, for facts the user may need such as provider DNS servers.
note.markdownDescription: One sentence shown under the *IPTV connection* page, for facts the user may need such as provider DNS servers.

sourceRanges.description: Unicast source networks multicast video may originate from. Used as altnet by igmpproxy only; improxy ignores it. Multicast group addresses are destinations and are not allowed here.
sourceRanges.markdownDescription:
Unicast source networks multicast video may originate from. Written as `altnet` lines for **igmpproxy only**; `improxy` has no equivalent and ignores it.

Multicast groups such as `224.0.0.0/4` are destinations, not source networks. Do not list them in `sourceRanges` or `natDestinations`.

provider.description: A TV brand. The wizard offers it in every listed country and then offers its profiles.
provider.markdownDescription: A TV brand. The wizard offers it in every listed country and then offers its profiles.

countries.description: Countries where this provider is offered. Each code must exist in countries.
countries.markdownDescription: Countries where this provider is offered. Each code must exist in `countries`.

name.description: Brand name as subscribers know it.
name.markdownDescription: Brand name as subscribers know it, for example `Telekom MagentaTV`.

profiles.description: Profile IDs this provider can use, in the order the wizard shows them. The first is the default. Each ID must exist in profiles.
profiles.markdownDescription:
Profile IDs this provider can use, in the order the wizard shows them. **The first is the default.** Each ID must exist in `profiles`.

With one entry the wizard skips the profile question.

ptrSuffixes.description: Reverse-DNS suffixes of this provider's customer addresses, matched on label boundaries. Only a low-confidence hint for the wizard.
ptrSuffixes.markdownDescription:
Reverse-DNS suffixes of this provider's customer addresses, matched on label boundaries: `kpn.net` matches `customer.kpn.net` and nothing else.

Only a low-confidence hint that pre-selects the provider in the wizard.

items.patternErrorMessage: Use a lowercase DNS suffix such as kpn.net.

wan.description: How the IPTV uplink is brought up on the provider-facing port.
wan.markdownDescription:
How the IPTV uplink is brought up on the provider-facing port.

`dhcp: true` forbids `staticAddress`; `dhcp: false` forbids `dhcpOptions`.

dhcp.description: true: obtain the IPTV address with udhcpc. false: bring the interface up with staticAddress, or without an address when omitted. https://github.com/armcc/udhcp/raw/refs/heads/master/README.udhcpc
dhcp.markdownDescription:
`true`: obtain the IPTV address with [`udhcpc`](https://github.com/armcc/udhcp/raw/refs/heads/master/README.udhcpc).

`false`: bring the interface up with `staticAddress`, or without an address when omitted.

dhcpOptions.description: Extra udhcpc arguments, one token per item. Only with dhcp true.
dhcpOptions.markdownDescription: Extra `udhcpc` arguments, one token per item, for example `["-O", "staticroutes", "-V", "IPTV_RG"]`. Only with `dhcp: true`.

items.patternErrorMessage: One token per item: a single-letter flag such as -O or a plain value such as staticroutes.

interface.description: Physical port or PPP interface carrying IPTV. Omit it; the console detects the port and the user picks it in the wizard.
interface.markdownDescription:
Physical port or PPP interface carrying IPTV. Omit it; the console detects the port and the user picks it in the wizard.

Set it only when the provider dictates it, such as `ppp0` for MagentaTV. `eth8.N` names a sub-interface of the detected port.

natDestinations.description: Unicast destinations reached through the IPTV uplink. Each becomes an iptables MASQUERADE rule matching on destination. Never list multicast groups here.
natDestinations.markdownDescription:
Unicast destinations reached through the IPTV uplink (guide, video on demand, DNS). Each becomes an `iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -d <cidr> -o <iptv> -j MASQUERADE` rule, matching on **destination**.

Never list multicast groups here or in `sourceRanges`; group forwarding is managed through receiver memberships.

staticAddress.description: Fixed IPv4 address with prefix length for the IPTV interface. Only with dhcp false.
staticAddress.markdownDescription: Fixed IPv4 address with prefix length for the IPTV interface, for example `10.20.30.1/24`. Only with `dhcp: false`.

vlan.description: 802.1Q VLAN ID for IPTV on the uplink, 1 to 4094. 0 means untagged.
vlan.markdownDescription: 802.1Q VLAN ID for IPTV on the uplink, 1 to 4094. `0` means untagged: no VLAN interface is created.

title: udm-iptv provider catalog
description: Countries, TV providers and the network profiles udm-iptv applies for each. The wizard asks country, then provider, then profile. Profiles are pure network settings; providers and countries only exist to find the right profile.
markdownDescription:
Countries, TV providers and the network profiles `udm-iptv` applies for each.

The wizard asks **country → provider → profile**. Profiles are pure network settings; providers and countries only exist to find the right profile.

Cross-references (`providers[].countries`, `providers[].profiles`) are checked by the Go loader, not by this schema.

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema, for editor validation.
$schema.markdownDescription: Path or URL of this schema, for editor validation.

countries.description: Markets with at least one provider, keyed by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.
countries.markdownDescription: Markets with at least one provider, keyed by **ISO 3166-1 alpha-2** code (`NL`, `CH`, …). Every country must be listed by at least one provider.

profiles.description: Network settings, keyed by profile ID. The ID is persisted in config.json, so never rename an existing one.
profiles.markdownDescription:
Network settings, keyed by profile ID.

The ID is persisted in `config.json` as `profile` and used by legacy-config inference, so **never rename an existing ID**. Every profile must be referenced by at least one provider.

providers.description: Brands a subscriber recognizes, keyed by ID. Each maps to one or more profiles.
providers.markdownDescription:
Brands a subscriber recognizes, keyed by ID. Each maps to one or more profiles.

Several providers may share one profile (KPN, XS4ALL and Freedom all use `kpn`). One provider may offer several profiles (Vivo: `vivo`, `vivogvt`).

schemaVersion.description: Catalog format version. A binary refuses a catalog with a version it does not know.
schemaVersion.markdownDescription: Catalog format version. A binary refuses a catalog with a version it does not know.
